title: The Battle of Tours
description: October 732. Charles Martel's Frankish infantry must hold the wooded high ground between Tours and Poitiers against the Umayyad cavalry of Abd al-Rahman. A third force of Aquitanian allies under Duke Odo can be rallied to strike the enemy camp. Victory requires repelling the cavalry charges and forcing the invaders' withdrawal.

anachronisms_found: Player One's leader is WILLIAM_THE_CONQUEROR, a mounted Norman hero of 1066, standing in for Charles Martel — and mounted, which contradicts the scenario's own 'shield wall' of dismounted Frankish infantry
Player Two's leader is SALADIN (d. 1193, Ayyubid Egypt/Syria) representing the Umayyad emir Abd al-Rahman al-Ghafiqi of 732 — over four centuries and a different dynasty removed

Player Three's leader is EL_CID (Castilian, d. 1099) representing Duke Odo of Aquitaine — wrong century and wrong polity, and an odd choice given El Cid fought Muslim and Christian rulers in Iberia, not Umayyad invaders in Gaul

KNIGHT units in the Umayyad roster: heavy Western-style lancers for an Arab-Berber raiding army; the engine offers Camel Rider, Light Cavalry and Cavalry Archer, which are used elsewhere in the roster, so the Knights were avoidable
PIKEMAN (a 14th-century weapon system) among the Frankish line where SPEARMAN/MILITIA/MAN_AT_ARMS would have sufficed

A full economic/military base for the Franks (TOWN_CENTER, BLACKSMITH, MONASTERY, ARCHERY_RANGE, two GUARD_TOWERS) on what the text describes as an improvised wooded ridge position — the Franks fought from a field formation, not a fortified settlement
